rules.name: Fair Housing Act - Familial Status Discrimination
rules.statuteSummary: The Fair Housing Act strictly prohibits discrimination based on familial status, including lease clauses banning children, restricting minors without safety justification, or imposing per-child penalty fees.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under the federal Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. § 3604), residential leases cannot discriminate on the basis of familial status. The restriction regarding children or minors in this clause is void under federal law.

rules.name: Fair Housing Act - Assistance & Service Animals
rules.statuteSummary: Landlords must make reasonable accommodations in rules or policies for individuals with disabilities, including permitting verified service and emotional support animals without charging pet rent or pet deposit fees.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under 42 U.S.C. § 3604(f)(3)(B) and federal HUD regulations, assistance and service animals are not pets and cannot be subjected to pet deposits, pet rent, or categorical no-pet bans.

rules.name: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) - Military Early Termination
rules.statuteSummary: Active-duty military personnel who receive deployment or permanent change of station (PCS) orders have the federal right to terminate a residential lease without liquidated damages or early termination penalties.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under 50 U.S.C. § 3955 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act), servicemembers have an unconditional federal right to terminate a residential lease upon receiving qualifying military orders without penalty.

rules.name: Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act
rules.statuteSummary: Federal law requires landlords renting residential housing built prior to 1978 to disclose known lead-based paint hazards and provide an EPA-approved information pamphlet before signing.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under 42 U.S.C. § 4852d, if the property was constructed prior to 1978, the landlord must provide a lead disclosure statement and EPA disclosure pamphlet.
